column1: Choose milk for a mild flavor or buttermilk for a lightly tangy variation. Stir the flour, sugar, baking powder, and salt together in a large bowl; add the baking soda only if using buttermilk. Make a well in the center.
Whisk the milk or buttermilk, melted butter, vanilla, and egg, then gently fold into the dry ingredients until no dry flour remains. Small lumps are fine; do not overmix.
If the batter is too thick to pour, thin it with a tablespoon or two of your chosen milk at a time; buttermilk may need a little more.
Let the batter rest while a nonstick pan or griddle heats over low-medium heat.
Wipe the pan with a little butter, pour in 1/4 cup batter per pancake, and gently spread into a round.
Cook about 2 minutes until the underside is golden, bubbles form on top, and the edges begin to set. Flip and cook 1–2 minutes more until golden and cooked through.
Repeat with the remaining batter and serve warm with your favorite toppings.
